summary: William Witherle Lawrence studied at Harvard University (~1899–1903). He held posts at Bowdoin College (~1898–1899) and Harvard University (~1900–1903), and taught Joseph Campbell.

Working in Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, William Woodville Rockhill studied at Lycée Condorcet, École Spéciale Militaire de Saint-Cyr (~1871–1873), and under Léon Feer and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux (~1876–1880).

Linguist William Wright studied at St Andrews, Halle, and Leiden. He taught Arabic at UCL and held posts at Trinity College, Hartford, Trinity College Dublin, the British Museum, and the University of Cambridge as Adams Professor of Arabic (1870–1889).

Indologist Willibald Kirfel completed his PhD and habilitation at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He worked at Bonn University Library (1911–1921) and served as ordentlicher Professor at the University of Bonn from 1922, succeeding Jacobi.

Sinologist Wilt L. Idema studied at Leiden University under Anthony François Paulus Hulsewé, as well as at Hokkaido and Kyoto universities. He served as Professor of Chinese Literature at Leiden (1976–1999) and at Harvard University (2000–2013).
Win Than Tun, a scholar in history and archaeology, studied at the National University of Singapore under Myo Myint.
A specialist in linguistics and Indology, Winfred P. Lehmann studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1937–1941). He was Professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (~1986–2007).
Working in Indology and linguistics, Winfred Robert Martin served as Professor of Oriental Languages at Trinity College, Hartford, and as Librarian at the Hispanic Society of America.

Wing-tsit Chan studied at Harvard University (~1924–1929) and worked in philosophy and Sinology. He held academic posts at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1935–1942), Dartmouth College (~1942–1966), and Chatham University (~1966–1982).

A religious studies scholar, Sullivan earned degrees from Cornell and the University of Chicago. She held posts at Washington and Lee, Chicago, University at Buffalo, and Indiana University Bloomington.
Specializing in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies, Winston Kyan earned his PhD from the University of Chicago, where he studied under Linda Seidel and doctoral supervisor Hung Wu.

Wolf Singer studied at the University of Munich (~1965–1968). He held posts at the Technical University of Munich, Goethe University Frankfurt, Max Planck Institute for Brain Research (~1981–2011), and Ernst Strüngmann Institute (~2008).

Wolfgang Franke, working in Sinology and history, studied at the University of Hamburg and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Sichuan and Peking universities and held the sinology chair at Hamburg (~1950–1977), succeeding Otto Franke.

Wolfgang Morgenroth studied at Jena under Richard Hauschild and completed his habilitation at Greifswald. He held teaching posts at Jena and Greifswald, and was Professor of Indology at Humboldt University of Berlin (1972–1994).

Wolfgang Schultz earned his PhD at the University of Vienna (~1900–1904). He worked at the Forschungsinstitut für Osten und Orient (1918–1921) and served as Professor and Chair of Philosophy at the University of Munich in 1934.

Wolfram Eberhard studied at Berlin under Ferdinand Lessing. He taught at several universities in China, worked at the Grassi and Berlin ethnological museums, and served as professor at Ankara University (1937–1948) and UC Berkeley (1948–1976).
Woncheol Yun, a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at Stony Brook University and served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University (attested 2012).
Woosung Huh, working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD from the University of Hawaiʻi and served as a professor of philosophy at Kyung Hee University (attested 2012).

Wu Mi studied at Tsinghua University and Harvard University, where he studied under Irving Babbitt. He worked in Sinology and held posts at Nanjing University (~1921–1924), Tsinghua University (~1925–1944), and Sichuan University (~1946–1949).
Wulstan Fletcher is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Taklung Tsetrul Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (both attested 1999).
